title: Who held which powers?
hook: Which offices exercised which powers in each regency?

knows: Selected accounts can describe distinct institutions and dated changes.
doesNotKnow: Ottoman regencies and local administrative autonomy

objective: Ottoman regencies and local administrative autonomy

claims.text: Kavas dates Tunis’s military dayi office to 1591, names Ibrahim first and Osman later, and distinguishes the bey’s tax/security work and beylerbeyi.
No timeless autonomy or all later Yusuf/Murad arrangements backdated 1591. Kavas Turkish scholarship, originals uncollated.
1591 Tunis Ibrahim First dayi Later Osman Bey Tax/security Beylerbeyi distinct Kavas scholarship Working English Original chronicles uncollated
Kavas dates Tripoli’s Ottoman conquest to 1551 and Turgut’s governorship to 1556; governor councils/jurists and competing elected dayis describe distinct institutions.
Conquest does not create every office instantly. Karamanli dynasty outside scope unselected; council/jurists not universal representation. Originals uncollated.
1551 Tripoli Conquest 1556 Turgut governor Council/jurists Elected dayis compete Kavas scholarship Working English Original chronicles uncollated
Tunis allocated fiscal/security work to the bey and military work to the dayi; Tripoli’s governor led tax patrols without timar.

claims.text: Kavas distinguishes Tunis’s military dayi, fiscal/security bey and governor from Tripoli’s governor, council, competing dayis and tax patrols. The accounts describe different local allocations of power under Ottoman affiliation. Conquest dates do not show every office appearing at once; councils and appointments neither imply universal representation nor establish timeless autonomy.
